notes.title: Dev Blog
notes.content:
[h2]Moin Moin[/h2]

We've made some exciting changes and improvements that we don't want to keep from you. Here are the details of the latest update:

[list]
[*] We have introduced a new module, the RTG. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40856210/927e06c4c10b3494cf4099daff0bb41c0beb9b36.png[/img]
This module produces and stores power and replaces the battery in the Pioneer from the outset when the distance to the sun is great, for example in orbit around Mars. The RTG module uses the new resource ‘Radioactive Isotopes’ for operation. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40856210/29b65c009dc7d4be7b53b6cea92fec0c110e8d53.png[/img]
These isotopes can be found on asteroids.

[*] Another new feature is that residents can now be moved manually between living quarters. This gives you more flexibility in managing your settlement.
[*]We have also added side quests. Smaller quests may appear from time to time, offering additional challenges and rewards. 
Note: Currently there are still few side quests, but we are working on adding more.
[/list]

notes.title: Dev Blog
notes.content:
[h2]Moin Moin[/h2]

We're thrilled to roll out one of our most substantial updates yet for Heliopolis Six. We've been
hard at work incorporating loads of new content and enhancements, and we're excited to share
these improvements with you. This update focuses on several key areas, thanks to your invaluable
feedback:

[list]
[*]Prestige System Overhaul: We've revamped the entire prestige mechanic, transitioning from
reputation points to a more dynamic prestige system, complete with new licensing fees and
implications for your gameplay.
[*]Enhanced Camera Controls: Navigate your space station like never before with our updated
camera settings. Enjoy the freedom of the new orbit mode and easily switch to free mode with a
press of the shift key.
[*]New Tutorial: New to our universe or needing a refresher? Our completely redesigned tutorial will
get you up to speed in no time, ensuring a smoother start for all commanders.
[*]Exciting New Station Parts: Expand your station with several new components, including various
braces and a brand new L-type part, all designed to increase your station's capabilities and
efficiency.
[/list]

Please bear with us if you encounter any textual errors in this update; we're continuously working
to refine and perfect the game's language. Your ongoing support and feedback have been
instrumental in shaping this update, and we're grateful for your contribution to our community.
Dive in and explore the new features - we can't wait to see the innovative stations you'll build!

notes.title: Patch Notes - v0.3.2/a05
notes.content:
Moin, 

we have made a few changes.

[h2]Fixed bugs[/h2]
[list]
    [*] Resource Views: Fixed issues with pipe’s resource specificity on special occasions.
    [*] Graphical Glitches: Corrected earth clouds appearing in front of the moon.
    [*] Turret Building Rotation
    [*] Fixed issue where deconstruction of stations parts could get stuck when there were modules inside.
[/list]

[h2]Changes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Pioneer Model optimisations: Reduced disk storage usage, updated appearance.
[*] You can now cancel research tasks.
[*] Cost Dependency: Construction costs for pipe tracks and cables are now lengthdependent.
[*] Increased max length for pipe, heat pipe and cable segments.
[*] Cable connector can now support up to 5 cables at batteries and solar arrays.
[*] Maintenance Module: Efficiency independent of station parts integrity, minimum of 20% efficiency when unpowered.
[*] Prestige System:[list]
[*] Renamed Reputation to Prestige.
[*] Removed Reputation Points.
[*] Licensing now requires initial credits and a recurring license fee per item used, payable daily.
[*] If the Prestige towards a company falls below the initial Prestige cost of a station part or module, it is not constructible as long as this is the case.[/list]
[*] Marketplace Renamed to Market.
[*] Resident Satisfaction: Moved from the bottom menu to the resident tooltip.
[*] Navigation and Camera Handling:
[*] Camera no longer moves automatically when selecting a station part, can be reenabled in settings.
[*] Camera is always in orbit mode, switchable to free mode by holding the shift key.
[*] Added 'H' and 'G' keys for home view.
[*] You can’t use the overview it there is no running scanner.
[*] Free mode is switched of when zooming out into overview.
[*] Wages: Now paid on a daily basis.
[*] Credit Balance: Interest accrues daily if balance falls below zero. Game lost when credits drop below -100k or all residents leave.
[*] Processes: Water cleaning, Algae growing an Making Food from Algae now need less power.
[*] Living quarter now shows if it is heating.
[*] When building a station part or a module, the stored and reserved* resources are shown. (* by other construction tasks)
[/list]

[h2]New features[/h2]
[list]
[*] Overhauled Tutorial: A completely revamped tutorial to enhance beginner experience,
    including six new scenarios in various locations for new challenges.
[*] New Quest Menu: Featuring a streamlined task display.
[*] New Station Parts:
[list]
    [*] Heat Decoupler
    [*] Various Braces: Medium Long Brace, Long Brace, L-Brace, T-Brace, X-Brace, TXBrace
    [*] L-Type Station Part
[/list]
[*] New mineable resource: Space Debris, mineable similarly to ore but found on drifting scrap,
not asteroids.
[/list]

[h2]Various[/h2]
[list]
    [*] Warning in Settings: If not all keys are assigned.
    [*] Added company filter in Prestige Menu.
    [*] Changed station part selection shader.
    [*] Removed top menu quest button.
    [*] Saving/Loading optimisations and fixes.
[/list]

notes.title: Dev Blog
notes.content:
[h2]Moin Moin[/h2]

With the latest patch, the revised research menu and new research options were introduced. You no longer have to click through the marketplace to get to the research assignments. The new basic research offers the possibility to improve modules or station parts.

The next major change will affect the search for minable objects.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40856210/0efad72a045a9bf0663da4dfd427fed9ebf40055.gif[/img]
We are working on a new station part that will allow you to scan the space around the station for these objects. This scanner will be able to operate with two processes: searching for objects and examining objects to determine their nature.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40856210/218eb76e8706dbc144b11288aec077a7ef04f6bc.gif[/img]
Once the scanner has found an object, it can be marked for mining as usual. The scanner has a limited range, which can be extended by building several scanners.

In addition, we are revising the tutorial. It will be divided into several missions and offers a first small insight into the backstory of H6. This will be the kickoff for the planned campaign.

Oh, and one more thing: We renamed this news to “dev blog”. Sometimes, there just isn't enough to report in a week. But don't worry, you will still get regular updates.

Stay tuned!

notes.title: Weekly News
notes.content:
[h2]Moin Moin[/h2]

Something has changed in the experimental branch.

First of all, a small thing:
The water that the station inhabitants consume is now mixed directly into the food. This means that the food processor needs much more water and also works twice as long, but the inhabitants now only consume food and oxygen. 

The more extensive change is the way other languages can be added to the game. When the game is started, a CSV file is created (in the folder "local path to the game"\Heliopolis Six\Heliopolis Six_Data\GameData\Languages) that contains all languages. This file can then be edited (change or add languages), Heliopolis Six should recognise this and will try to apply the changes. Once the CSV file has been created, it is always used and no new one is created.
So far, the file contains English, German and French. The French translation is probably very bad, as we only have a very rudimentary knowledge of French.

We hope for your help with the translations. If you feel like it, you can send us your edited CSV by mail or via Discord.

Next we will work on a new view that will visualise the flow of resources.

See you then.

notes.title: Weekly News
notes.content:
[h2]Moin Moin[/h2]

We have introduced an experimental branch for Heliopolis Six.
You can activate it in your library. Right click on the game -> properties -> betas and there select beta in beta participation. There you can also find the previous version, in case something is wrong with the current one.


In the experimental branch you can now find some changes:

As already announced, the assistant system has been removed. However, the respective functions of the assistants have remained and are available right from the start.

Assigning residents to their jobs now happens automatically. this can also be turned on and off individually and is controlled by priorities.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40856210/037f249ac7a172d494a8bc64fd1cec672e3c7480.png[/img]

Furthermore, we have introduced the possibility to lock the camera in orbit or free mode. The function was there before, but it was always overridden by the automatic mode. There are two new buttons for this in the upper right corner and the corresponding keyboard assignment in the settings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40856210/4eda2f004ab5bc4dd718e2036f361c135965a1f3.png[/img]

Otherwise, we introduced credits in the main menu, so the splash screen at the start of the game only contains the Acid Mines logo and is shorter. 
And the heat production of the living quarters has been increased so that the residents don't freeze to death so quickly.

Some of the changes we would like to test further and get feedback from you players before the experimental version goes to the standard version. 
Then there will be patch notes for the version.

See you next week.

notes.title: Weekly News
notes.content:
[h2]Moin Moin[/h2]

We are back again! Hopefully the last weeks were as relaxing for you as they were for us.

In the last two weeks we were able to fix some bugs in the game, most of which were found by you. Thanks for the bug reports here, they really mean a lot to us.

We have also changed the algorithm that optimizes the flow of fluid resources through the station. The model we use has always been based on the Euler equations of fluid dynamics and we have now incorporated the influence of momentum. The end result is that changes propagate faster and resources get where they need to go faster.

Until now, the flow of resources through pipes and cables was also calculated this way. But there should always have been another system. That is what has happened now. The maximum flow through the pipes and cables is still limited, but it is calculated directly between the connected storages. So it doesn't matter how long the pipe or cable is (which is not the case for the flow through the station), the resources are much faster. Thus, the pipes and cables are even more important for larger stations.

Next, we would like to take on resident micromanagement. We've gotten a lot of feedback that managing residents and their jobs is too much and too unclear. 
The assignment of residents will happen automatically, but you will still be able to manually control who works where. 
The assistance system will probably be dropped and the corresponding bonuses (e.g. automatic repair) will be permanently available. 
There will also soon be a new view that visualizes resource flows.

If you have any ideas for changes or improvements, feel free to contact us.
See you next week.

Next, we will introduce a warning system that will alert you when life support is about to fail or other hazards appear. 
In addition to the obligatory text message, there will also be an acoustic signal.

At the same time, we are trying to improve the resident menu and the menu for the research tasks.

Until next week

notes.title: Keyboard Layout and a new dropdown menu
notes.content:
Moin, 

it may not be much, but these are the main new features from this week's patch.

[list]
[*] There is now the possibility to freely assign all functions  to the keyboard as desired. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40856210/f0dda258a03a5f12465e420149ba03ce5730843a.gif[/img]


[*] The selection of processes is now done by a dropdown menu. We think that is clearer and a little more intuitive. Also, there is now the possibility to influence the maximum efficiency a module.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40856210/7ebdde20bb46c2451d889964bf05451be1a453ea.gif[/img]


[*] Furthermore, there are now additional status icons in the management menu of the station parts. It is displayed when workstations are not occupied, no process is selected and if there are problems with the resources.

notes.title: Patch Notes - v0.3.1/d01
notes.content:
Moin, 

we have made a few changes and introduced something new.

[h2]New Features[/h2]
[list]
[*] In the settings, all functions can now be freely assigned to the keyboard as desired.
[*] Status icons have been added to the module icons in the station part management menu.
They indicate that workstations are not occupied or only partially occupied, if there are problems with the resource supply or if no production process is selected at all.
[*] The slowest speed can be switched with the space bar and the game speed can be adjusted with + and -. This keyboard layout can also be changed.
[*] The maximum efficiency with which a module should produce can be set. (This can be very useful in the event of power shortage)
[/list]

[h2]Bug Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Fixed that the camera continues to move when the quest menu opens and the camera was moved.
[*] Fixed that the game sometimes partially freezes when building power lines.
[*] The calculation of resource flows has been reworked so that unnatural bottlenecks should no longer occur.
[/list]

[h2]Changes[/h2]
[list]
[*] The selection of processes is now done by a dropdown menu.
[*] In the pioneer station part, the battery is now visible.
[*] When the quest menu is closed, the game speed is set to normal.
[/list]

[*] The planets Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune can no longer be selected.
[/list]
